title: On the Alignment between Fairness and Accuracy: from the Perspective of Adversarial Robustness
headline: Open finding: under the universal ordinary-DP reading of Corollary 4.1, unequal label base rates refute its multiplicative comparison with equalized odds.

work.title: On the Alignment between Fairness and Accuracy: from the Perspective of Adversarial Robustness
work.venue: Proceedings of the 42nd International Conference on Machine Learning (PMLR)

claims.label: Corollary 4.1 quantitative demographic-parity/equalized-odds comparison
claims.gist: Corollary 4.1 states an adversarial quantitative comparison of ordinary demographic-parity and equalized-odds disparities; its constants and dependence are not specified.
claims.statement: Under the natural universal reading that a positive multiplicative constant compares the ordinary demographic-parity and equalized-odds objectives for all admitted score configurations, Corollary 4.1 is false when group label base rates differ.
conditions: The paper defines ordinary demographic parity as the absolute gap in groups' overall average scores.
Equalized odds is the sum of absolute within-label group-score gaps.
Corollary 4.1 states a multiplicative comparison without an equal-base-rate or balancing condition.
claims.quantifiers: The quantitative comparison is read as applying to all score configurations admitted by the paper; the eight-observation witness has all four cells nonempty and unequal label base rates.

result.summary: Unequal base rates yield ordinary DP equal to 0.5 while EOd is zero, including at the maximum of the stated DP attack under the natural universal reading.
result.witness: Use eight observations with cell counts |S00|=3, |S10|=1, |S01|=1, |S11|=3, and assign score 0 to every Y=0 observation and 1 to every Y=1 observation. Then mu00=mu01=0, mu10=mu11=1, L_EOd=0, and L_DP=|3/4-1/4|=1/2. A smooth classifier with separated feature centers can keep these scores fixed under every allowed perturbation, so maximizing the stated DP objective still gives DP=1/2 and EOd=0.
result.argument: For any positive constant c, the proposed universal inequality L_EOd >= c L_DP would require 0 >= c/2, which is false. All four cells are nonempty, with no threshold ties or zero-radius perturbation. Appendix D's label-balanced contrast remains distinct from the ordinary DP gap defined in Equation (1).
not_claimed: The finding is conditional on the natural universal reading of the unspecified multiplicative constants.
The label-balanced Appendix D contrast and other paper results are not challenged.
No separate implication under additional saturation conventions is ruled out.
result.repair_note: State an equal-base-rate or other balancing condition, or formulate the bound for the label-balanced contrast controlled by Appendix D.

vor_check.pages: Equation (1) and Corollary 4.1, printed p. 4; Appendix D, printed p. 14
vor_check.detail: Equation (1), Corollary 4.1, and Appendix D were checked in the official rendered PMLR Version of Record PDF. The source level is full.

evidence.detail: A fresh hostile reconstruction checked the decisive witness against the source and recorded its scope and nonclaims.
An independent senior AI review in a separate read-only session confirmed the narrowly stated finding; this is not human verification.

claims.novelty: A bounded search found no correction or independent public identification of the precise Corollary 4.1 issue. On printed p. 9 (PMLR p. 7115), the paper separately notes in an accuracy-attack discussion that EOd can be zero while DP remains nonzero because of base-rate disparities; that related observation is not presented there as a correction to Corollary 4.1. OpenReview discussion could not be inspected because its forum endpoint returned an access challenge; unindexed discussion is not excluded.
